title: Bijectivity of the affine pure-tensor sections map
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $V\subseteq Y$ and $U\subseteq X$ affine opens with $U\subseteq f^{-1}V$, $A=\mathcal O_Y(V)$ and $B=\mathcal O_X(U)$ with its $A$-algebra structure induced by $f$. Let $G$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and use the specified tensor-formula pullback and its specified adjunction unit [def-pc-module-pullback], [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. Any $A$-linear map $c:G(V)\otimes_A B\to(f^*G)(U)$ satisfying $c(s\otimes b)=b\,\eta_f(s)|_U$ for every $s\in G(V)$ and $b\in B$ is bijective.

proof.text: Restrict G to N on Spec A. Quasi-coherence is preserved by restriction. The inverse restriction maps identify Gamma(N) with G(V), as A-modules, and Gamma((standard f*G)|Spec B) with (standard f*G)(U), as B-modules.

Use the already-proved standard-pullback implementation of the affine tilde-Gamma counit and tilde base change: pullbackSpecΓEquiv rho N from WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.Modules.PullbackTilde is a B-linear equivalence from extension of scalars of Gamma(N) to Gamma(psi*N). Its one-tensor formula is pullbackSpecΓEquiv_one_tmul. This realizes Schemes 01I9/01IA/01HV for the standard left adjoint.

Identify the right adjoints of the two routes through the chart square. Their unique left-adjoint comparison k is an isomorphism. Compose its map on global sections with the section identifications of step 1, the equivalence of step 2, the tensor swap and the native-tensor/ModuleCat extension-of-scalars equivalence. This is a bijection.

Identify the specified tensor pullback with the standard pullback by uniqueness of left adjoints. The unit equation, its naturality with restriction, and chart-unit compatibility show on s tensor b that the transported c equals the composite bijection: first reduce b tensor s to b times (1 tensor s), then use the one-tensor formula of step 2 and chart-unit compatibility. Tensor induction extends equality over zero and sums. Injectivity and surjectivity now follow from the component equivalences.
